guitar.notes: Mick Jones plays a mix of Les Pauls and Stratocasters; no single ultra-iconic guitar, medium is accurate.

tone.target: anthemic 80s arena rock crunch with chorus sheen and short delay
tone.profile: anthemic 80s arena rock crunch with chorus sheen and short delay
tone.summary: A classic 80s arena rock chain using light overdrive for grit, a Marshall-style amp for punch, chorus for sheen, and delay/room for big stereo depth.

rig.name: Foreigner - Juke Box Hero - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide light, bright crunch and sustain for the 80s rock tone.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general choice; Blues OD or Boost could also work but Green OD offers better mid-range punch.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No dedicated distortion needed as Green OD handles the crunch).
Simulate the punchy, mid-forward sound of a Marshall-style 80s rock amp.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is the best fit for classic British crunch. Using US Deluxe would be an alternative if a more American tone was desired.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary high-end punch.
Add the required 'chorus sheen' and stereo width characteristic of 80s arena rock.
Add a subtle, short delay for depth without muddying the mix.
blocks.gap: The Digital Delay is versatile. Slapback could be used if only very short repeats were desired.

blocks.purpose: Create a big stereo feel and natural ambience suitable for arena rock.
Slightly boost the mids and highs while reducing low-end mud to combat mid-scoop.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and high-end definition for an authentic 80s arena rock sheen.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, punchy high-end required for 80s sheen.
